parsed.attack: Tandem's medication-management app [47] is the closest death and the most damning: a daily adherence log for patients on multi-drug regimens, where missing a day has clinical consequences, whose team validated the need in research, launched, found retention "really difficult" and stopped. If a daily log cannot hold people whose health depends on it, it does not hold seventeen-year-olds recording optional practice drives. Habitual [63] supplies the second half - a streak tracker in a saturated category that never found a channel - and this product is strictly harder than either, because it needs two installs per household with the parent countersigning, which is why its own first kill criterion is a coin flip on whether the loop exists at all.
parsed.strongest_defence: The countersign is the product: the streak is witnessed by the person in the passenger seat rather than self-reported, and free per-session grading turns a compliance log into something that gives the learner feedback, which is the one thing neither Tandem nor Habitual ever offered.
parsed.verdict_reason: A clinically motivated daily log already died of retention and a streak tracker already died of having no channel, and free on-device grading dissolves neither while the two-sided install makes both worse.
